claims.text: The initial AlCoFeNi alloy is relatively uniform and single-phase B2 in the as-cast or homogenized condition.
The intervention replaces about half of the Co in AlCoFeNi with Cr to produce AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi.
Partial substitution of Co by Cr promotes separation into a B2 matrix and fine Cr-rich BCC precipitates.
Fine Cr-rich BCC precipitates act as domain-wall-pinning sites.
Annealing near 600 °C favors hierarchical phase decomposition more strongly than annealing at higher temperatures.
The proposed microstructure consists of a B2 matrix containing fine BCC precipitates enriched in Fe-Co or compositionally altered by Cr.
Cr segregates at grain boundaries in the modified alloy.
The precipitates and Cr grain-boundary segregation increase magnetic inhomogeneity.
Cr has an antiferromagnetic character relevant to this AlCoFeNi-based alloy.
Substitution with Cr reduces the alloy's saturation magnetization.
Cr-rich regions create localized energy barriers that impede domain-wall motion.
Increased domain-wall pinning produces a higher coercive field.
AlCoFeNi annealed at 600 °C has a coercive field of approximately 14.5 Oe.
AlCoFeNi annealed at 600 °C has a saturation magnetization near 100 emu/g.
AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi annealed at 600 °C is expected to have a coercive field on the order of 39 Oe.
The Cr-substituted alloy is expected to have lower saturation magnetization than the matched AlCoFeNi baseline.
The coercivity increase should hold for arc-melted alloys subjected to controlled annealing that favors phase separation.
Changes in processing, composition, Cr distribution, or thermal history may alter phase stability, microstructure, and magnetic response.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis identifies the fine BCC precipitates as Cr-rich, whereas the structural-mediator field identifies them as Fe-Co-rich or only vaguely 'altered by Cr'; the proposed precipitate chemistry is therefore inconsistent.
